issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must establish continuous readiness and willingness to perform the essential terms of the contract.
material_facts: The buyer pleaded that he was ready and willing to perform and testified to that effect.
He paid substantial advances, produced evidence of funds and financial capacity, and corresponded with the bank about settlement of the debt.
The sellers did not show that they had demanded further payment from the buyer or that he had failed to respond to such a demand.
issues.conclusion: The buyer proved readiness and willingness, and the concurrent findings granting specific performance on this ground were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires the plaintiff to plead and prove continuous readiness and willingness to perform the essential terms of the contract. Readiness concerns financial capacity, while willingness is assessed from conduct. The court assesses the entirety of the facts and circumstances, including conduct before and after suit; no fixed formula applies. The plaintiff need not actually tender or deposit money unless directed by the court. The Court relied on N.P. Thirugnanam v. Dr. R. Jagan Mohan Rao, P. D'Souza v. Shondrilo Naidu, and R.C. Chandiok v. Chuni Lal Sabharwal.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and plaintiff_claims_contract_performance and (plaintiff_shows_financial_capacity and plaintiff_shows_consistent_willing_conduct) and not credible_contrary_evidence

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.plaintiff_claims_contract_performance: The plaintiff asserts that they have performed or are ready and willing to perform their essential contractual obligations.
predicates.plaintiff_shows_financial_capacity: The plaintiff produces evidence that they had the financial means to perform the payment obligations.
predicates.plaintiff_shows_consistent_willing_condu: The plaintiff's pleadings, payments, testimony, and other conduct show a continuing willingness to complete the contract.
predicates.credible_contrary_evidence: The opposing party produces credible evidence that the plaintiff was unable or unwilling to perform.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance plaintiff claims performance, shows financial capacity and consistent willingness, and faces no credible contrary evidence, specific performance may be granted.

issues.legal_issue: A contract to sell mortgaged property is not void as a contingent contract merely because discharge of the mortgage and delivery of title documents remain to be completed.
material_facts: The later sale agreement required the vendors to discharge the loans and hand over the title deeds, and allowed them to seek further advances from the buyer for that purpose.
The agreement did not make the bank's acceptance of a particular settlement offer a condition to the sale.
The buyer made substantial advance payments and had evidence of funds, while the sellers did not show that they had requested further advances or attempted to perform their obligations.
issues.conclusion: The contract was capable of performance, was not a contingent contract that had become void, and could support specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 31 and 32 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 define contingent contracts and provide that a contract contingent on an uncertain future event cannot be enforced before that event occurs and becomes void if the event becomes impossible. The Court held that the later agreement's terms did not make the bank's acceptance of a settlement offer a condition precedent to sale; clearing the loan and obtaining title deeds were capable contractual obligations and incidental steps to give effect to the agreement.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.contract_alleged_to_be_contingent: A party argues that the agreement depends on an uncertain event and is therefore unenforceable.
predicates.agreement_does_not_condition_sale_on_unc: The agreement does not make completion of the sale conditional on the occurrence of the asserted uncertain event.
predicates.contractual_obligations_remain_capable_o: The parties' obligations, including clearing an encumbrance and obtaining title documents, remain capable of performance.

issues.definition: When a contract is alleged to be contingent but does not condition the sale on an uncertain event and its obligations remain performable, it is not void as contingent.

issues.legal_issue: A subsequent purchaser who obtains a decree for specific performance may invoke marshalling to have a mortgage debt satisfied first from the mortgagor's unsold properties, even if that legal plea was not specifically raised at trial, provided the mortgagee's rights are not prejudiced.
material_facts: The sellers had mortgaged multiple properties to the bank and agreed to sell one of those properties to the buyer.
The buyer sought specific performance and had also sought relief requiring the sellers to discharge the loan; the trial court granted only part of the relief sought.

The buyer's pleadings and the related writ petition described the existence of other properties available for recovery, and the bank did not establish factual prejudice from resort to those properties first.
The bank did not appeal the High Court's direction, which preserved its right to proceed against the sold property if the other properties did not satisfy the debt.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to apply marshalling in the buyer's favour, notwithstanding that the doctrine had not been specifically pleaded at trial, while safeguarding the bank's rights.
issues.legal_principle: Section 56 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 gives a subsequent purchaser of one of multiple mortgaged properties a right, absent a contrary contract, to have the debt satisfied from the properties not sold to that purchaser so far as possible, without prejudicing the mortgagee or other protected interests. Section 81 addresses marshalling by a subsequent mortgagee. The Court treated marshalling as an equitable principle and a question of law arising from the decree and the relief claimed; it may be applied where the court moulds relief to achieve substantial justice. Any alleged prejudice to a mortgagee is a factual matter requiring pleading and proof. The Court relied on Sain Ditta Mal v. Bulagi Mal & Sons, Karam Singh Sobti v. Smt. Shukla Bedi, and Brahm Parkash v. Manbir Singh, and distinguished the pleading principles in Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy and Bachhaj Nahar v. Nilima Mandal.

rule.if: subsequent_purchaser_proceeding and purchaser_has_specific_performance_decree and mortgagor_has_multiple_mortgaged_properties and purchaser_acquired_one_property and other_properties_can_be_used_first and not proven_prejudice_to_mortgagee

predicates.subsequent_purchaser_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a purchaser who acquired an interest in property after the owner mortgaged multiple properties.
predicates.purchaser_has_specific_performance_decre: The purchaser has obtained a decree requiring conveyance of the purchased property.
predicates.mortgagor_has_multiple_mortgaged_propert: The owner mortgaged more than one property to secure the debt.
predicates.purchaser_acquired_one_property: The purchaser's interest concerns one or more, but not all, of the mortgaged properties.
predicates.other_properties_can_be_used_first: Other mortgaged properties remain available to satisfy the debt before resort to the property acquired by the purchaser.
predicates.proven_prejudice_to_mortgagee: The mortgagee proves that using the other properties first would prejudice its rights.

issues.definition: When a purchaser has a specific-performance decree for one of multiple mortgaged properties and other properties can satisfy the debt first without proven prejudice to the mortgagee, marshalling may be applied in the purchaser's favour.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court may hear a writ petition together with a regular first appeal when the proceedings concern the same parties, properties, and connected issues and no bar to doing so applies.
material_facts: The writ petition and the regular appeals concerned the same properties and substantially the same parties.
The issues in the writ petition were connected with those raised in the appeals.
No serious objection to hearing the proceedings together had been raised before the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not barred from hearing and disposing of the connected writ petition along with the regular appeals.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that there is no bar to a Division Bench with jurisdiction over an appeal hearing a connected writ petition where the same dispute and properties are involved. It also noted that the Supreme Court had earlier requested that the connected matters be disposed of together.

rule.if: regular_first_appeal and connected_writ_petition and same_core_dispute_and_properties and no_bar_to_joint_hearing

predicates.regular_first_appeal: The proceeding includes a regular first appeal before the High Court.
predicates.connected_writ_petition: A writ petition is pending that concerns issues connected with the appeal.
predicates.same_core_dispute_and_properties: The appeal and writ petition concern the same core dispute and properties.
predicates.no_bar_to_joint_hearing: No legal bar prevents the High Court from hearing the proceedings together.

issues.definition: When a regular first appeal and a connected writ petition concern the same dispute and properties, and no bar applies, the High Court may hear them together.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court may grant marshalling relief concerning mortgaged property without contradicting a debt recovery forum's recovery order when the relief preserves the creditor's ability to recover its debt.
material_facts: The High Court directed that other properties be proceeded against first, while allowing recovery against the property covered by the sale agreement if the other properties proved insufficient.
The bank was a party to the proceedings and did not appeal the High Court's decision.
The direction addressed the order in the specific-performance dispute and did not cancel the debt or the recovery entitlement.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's direction did not modify or erode the debt recovery forum's order and did not warrant interference.
issues.legal_principle: The Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 and the authorities concerning the jurisdiction of the recovery forum do not bar a civil court from granting a distinct equitable relief under Section 56 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, where that relief does not disturb the recovery order and safeguards the bank's ability to recover. The Court considered Allahabad Bank v. Canara Bank, State Bank of India v. Allied Chemical Laboratories, and India Household and Healthcare Ltd. v. LG Household and Healthcare Ltd.

predicates.civil_proceeding_concerning_mortgaged_pr: The civil proceeding concerns property that secures a debt owed to a creditor.
predicates.recovery_forum_has_order: A competent debt recovery forum has made an order for recovery of the debt.
predicates.civil_court_grants_distinct_relief: The civil court grants separate relief concerning the manner in which properties may be used to satisfy the debt.
predicates.creditor_retains_recovery_against_proper: The creditor remains able to recover against the property at issue if other available assets do not satisfy the debt.

issues.definition: When a civil court grants distinct relief but preserves recovery against the property if other assets are insufficient, that relief does not conflict with the recovery order.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff who pays substantial court fees and obtains the principal relief sought may be awarded costs despite not obtaining every requested form of relief.
material_facts: The plaintiff paid substantial court fees and obtained a decree for specific performance, the principal relief sought.
The plaintiff did not obtain all the additional relief requested.
issues.conclusion: The High Court properly awarded costs to the plaintiff against the contesting defendants.
issues.legal_principle: Section 35 of the Code of Civil Procedure governs costs. The Court upheld the award because the plaintiff paid substantial court fees and obtained the major relief sought, notwithstanding that the suit did not succeed in its entirety.

rule.if: civil_suit and plaintiff_paid_substantial_court_fees and plaintiff_obtained_principal_relief and not plaintiff_obtained_all_requested_relief

predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.plaintiff_paid_substantial_court_fees: The plaintiff paid substantial court fees for the relief claimed.
predicates.plaintiff_obtained_principal_relief: The plaintiff succeeded in obtaining the principal relief sought in the suit.
predicates.plaintiff_obtained_all_requested_relief: The plaintiff obtained every form of relief requested.

issues.definition: When a civil plaintiff pays substantial court fees and obtains the principal relief but not every requested remedy, the court may award costs to the plaintiff.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court's discretionary power under Article 136 continues after special leave is granted, and the Court need not interfere unless the case warrants intervention in the interests of justice.
material_facts: The appeals were heard after leave had been granted.
The Court considered the concurrent findings below and found no basis to disturb the result.
issues.conclusion: The Court retained discretion after grant of leave and dismissed the appeals, finding no ground warranting interference.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 confers discretionary jurisdiction that continues after special leave is granted. The Court need not decide every issue on the merits or interfere merely because an error is alleged; an appellant must show exceptional or special circumstances and that non-interference would result in substantial and grave injustice. The Court relied on Balvantrai Chimanlal Trivedi v. M. N. Nagrashna, Taherakhatoon v. Salambin Mohammad, and Chandra Singh v. State of Rajasthan.

predicates.appeal_under_article_136_after_leave: The proceeding is an appeal under the Supreme Court's special-leave jurisdiction after leave has been granted.
predicates.appellant_fails_to_show_exceptional_circ: The appellant does not establish exceptional or special circumstances warranting intervention.
predicates.no_substantial_grave_injustice_from_noni: The Court finds that declining to interfere would not cause substantial and grave injustice.

issues.definition: When an appeal after leave lacks exceptional circumstances and non-interference would not cause substantial and grave injustice, the Supreme Court may decline to interfere.
